Des Moines, Iowa Thu'). Negotiated base 36.70 on 2,863 head; net 36.34. roll5 41.63 is the mean of the five most recent PUBLISHED negotiated base prices held here (Nov 9 49.43, Nov 10 43.25, Nov 16 40.04, Nov 17 38.75, Nov 18 36.70); Nov 11-13 were never captured, so it spans Nov 9-18 rather than five consecutive sessions. low/high are NOT 2026-11-18 figures - the Nov 19 summary does not print LM_HG201's Lowest/Highest Net Lot, so 34.70/44.00 is still the 2026-11-17 dispersion. Reported but deliberately excluded from PI. || 2026-11-23 RUN: WHY THE 2026-11-20 FIGURES WERE NOT WRITTEN: the LM_HG201 prior-day report released 2026-11-23 (covering the 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21 slaughter) WAS obtained this session, but only through a single commercial aggregator's rendering, and that rendering FAILS an internal consistency test that the real report passes. Gaps of 0.19 and 0.27. Those cannot be explained by the 337 withheld negotiated-formula head: closing them would require a negotiated-formula base of 234.4 and a net of 317.0, which are impossible. The gap is NOT normal for this report - the same reconciliation run against the PRIMARY AMS document held from 2026-10-23 closes to 0.032 on the base and 0.037 on the net. So at least one price in the Nov 20 rendering is mis-parsed and there is no way from here to tell which. The head counts and carcass weights from the same report DID verify (they reconcile exactly, and two independent renderings agree), and the carcass weights were written; the prices were not. The AMS mnreports endpoints were re-checked and were AGAIN serving stale files - lsddhps.pdf printed 'Oct 23, 2026', ams_2498.pdf 'October 26, 2026', ams_2675.pdf 'October 20, 2026'. The Barchart S3 mirror that served the primary document on previous runs could not be reached this session. Per RUNBOOK the old value and its OLD asof date are kept for the gate to grade. Nothing was carried forward under today's date. For the record, had it verified, the Nov 20 reading would have been base 36.61 on 6,228 head with net 35.69 and a net-lot range of 29.91-41.20, which would have made roll5 39.07. The NET of 35.69 is in fact double-confirmed; it is the BASE that this block's 'value' field carries and that could not be verified. || 2026-11-24 RUN: STILL HELD at 2026-11-18. Packer-sold 34,031 head @ 55.91. National negotiated: low 28.00, high 37.00, wtd avg 31.77, change -0.36, 5-day rolling 32.82; Iowa/Minnesota 31.99, Western Cornbelt 31.64, Eastern Cornbelt 33.54. TESTS IT PASSES: (1) the five head counts sum to 209,105 + 170 = 209,275, EXACTLY the printed producer-sold total; (2) head-weighting the four priced types gives 56.1144 against the printed 56.10, a gap of 0.014, and closing it requires a withheld negotiated-formula base of about 38.2 on 170 head, which is entirely plausible - against the IMPOSSIBLE 234.4 the 2026-11-20 rendering required; (3) the printed -0.36 negotiated change chains exactly off the 32.13 the same publisher prints for 2026-11-20. WHY IT WAS STILL NOT WRITTEN: test (3) is same-source and tests (1) and (2) are self-consistency only - they rule out a column mis-parse but not a wrong table - and NO independent rendering was reachable. CUTOUT.src: LM_PK602 afternoon (FOB plant), 2026-11-19 PM: cutout 68.66, -0.82 from 69.48. Read from the PRIMARY source - the USDA AMS 'National Daily Hog and Pork Summary' whose printed header reads 'Nov 19, 2026 ... Des Moines, Iowa Thu'. Corroborated arithmetically: all SIX primals chain exactly off the independently confirmed 2026-11-18 values - Loin 68.40-2.17=66.23, Butt 97.19-1.22=95.97, Picnic 56.99+0.46=57.45, Rib 127.58+0.82=128.40, Ham 62.90-0.14=62.76, Belly 66.48-1.13=65.35 - and the cutout chains 69.48-0.82=68.66. Total loads 239.20 (pork cuts 208.84 + trim/process 30.36). || 2026-11-23 RUN: still held at 2026-11-19. A 2026-11-20 PM cutout of 67.88 WAS found, described as the lowest since August 2020, in an Ag Optimus COT piece published 2026-11-23 04:25 UTC. It is UNCORROBORATED and was NOT written in: it is a single source, no second rendering of the Nov 20 afternoon report was reachable, and unlike the Nov 19 figure there is no primal set to chain it against. That source was accurate on everything else it could be tested on this session (its Nov 20 Dec and Feb settlements match three other routes to the cent, and two of its lean-hog-index basis figures reconcile exactly), so 67.88 is probably right - but 'probably' is not the standard, and RUNBOOK is explicit that an unverified price is left for the gate to flag. It is recorded HERE, clearly labelled uncorroborated, so a later run can use it as a chain anchor if a second source turns up. The AMS mnreports endpoints were again stale (ams_2498.pdf printed 'October 26, 2026'; lsddhps.pdf 'Oct 23, 2026'), the Barchart S3 mirror was unreachable, no 2026-11-23 PM wire had published by run time, and ThePigSite's latest CME wire is still dated 2026-11-19. Separately, a weekly COMPREHENSIVE cutout of 71.04 dated 2026-11-16 was seen; that is a different series from the daily FOB-plant cutout and is not interchangeable with it. One cross-check worth noting: ThePigSite's 2026-11-18 wire printed the Nov 17 cutout as '66.44' while stating a change of -2.80 from Monday; 71.24-2.80=68.44, the value held here, so that wire has a digit transposition and the 68.44 in this file is confirmed correct. || 2026-11-24 RUN: HELD WHOLE at 2026-11-19, deliberately, even though the 2026-11-20 PM cutout is now FULLY CORROBORATED. 67.88 (-0.78) is confirmed by a Reuters/Global Ag Media CME wire published 2026-11-23 ("The wholesale pork carcass cutout value fell 78 cents on Friday to $67.88 per cwt, the USDA said, a six-year low"), which is a SECOND independent source for the Ag Optimus figure recorded in the note above, and it chains exactly: 68.66 - 0.78 = 67.88. WHY THE BLOCK DID NOT ADVANCE: this block's single asof labels BOTH the cutout and the primals (report.py renders "Pork cutout and primals" under CUTOUT['asof']). No 2026-11-20 primal breakdown was reachable from any route tried, so moving asof to 2026-11-20 would carry the 2026-11-19 primal set forward under a 2026-11-20 label - exactly the failure this file exists to prevent. The verified 67.88 was instead appended to CUTOUT_EXTRA, where every point carries its own date, so PI gets the datapoint in its history without any field being mislabelled. A LATER RUN THAT OBTAINS 2026-11-20 PRIMALS CAN ADVANCE THIS BLOCK IMMEDIATELY: value 67.88, prior 68.66, chg -0.78, asof 2026-11-20. The combined figure also reconciles ARITHMETICALLY: head-weighting the four types by the report's own head counts (6,228 / 31,737 / 171,282 / 107,061) gives 221.855 against the printed 221.88, and those head counts plus the 337 withheld negotiated-formula head sum to 316,645, exactly the printed producer-sold total. packer_owned 218.94 required adjudication: the two renderings SWAP the packer-owned and packer-sold labels (218.94 vs 222.89). Weights rising into late November is seasonally normal and consistent with wire commentary on heavier weights adding supply. LH_INDEX.note: 56.32 is the CME Lean Hog Index for 2026-11-18, the latest published as of the 2026-11-20 close (the index runs a two-business-day lag). Single-source on its face - an Ag Optimus COT piece published 2026-11-23 04:25 UTC - but it passes TWO independent arithmetic checks against figures verified here from other sources, which is why it is written in rather than held. The piece states the index stood $3.72 over December: 56.32 - 52.60 (the 2026-11-20 Dec settlement, independently confirmed by four sources) = 3.72 exactly. It states the comparable basis was $2.38 on 2026-11-16: 57.73 (the 2026-11-12 index held here) - 55.35 (the 2026-11-16 Dec close held here) = 2.38 exactly. Both checks reconcile to the cent against values this file already held, and the second also confirms the publication-lag convention. The 2026-11-17 index value was never published to a reachable source, so the series steps from 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-18 rather than being padded.
